name: Sir Dennis Gillings
current_role: Non-Executive Chair and Founder, GHO Capital (healthcare investment firm); retired IQVIA lead director (2018)
profile: British-born statistician (b. 1944, London) who co-founded Quintiles in Durham, NC, growing it from UNC biostatistics consulting into the world's largest clinical-research organisation; Quintiles merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Now an investor/chair at London-based GHO Capital and a dementia-research advocate.
interesting_fact: In 2014 David Cameron appointed him World Dementia Envoy; he helped found and became first chairman of the World Dementia Council, and was knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
deep_cut_fact: Quintiles traces back to a single 1974 project: Hoechst hired the UNC biostatistics professor to analyse trial data for a new diabetes drug; his analysis showed which patients to exclude, letting Hoechst bring it to market. The company was only incorporated in 1982 with fellow professor Gary Koch.
notes: Lane name 'Sir Dennis' = Sir Dennis Gillings (wealth shared with wife Mireille Gillings, per Sunday Times). Son of a London fishmonger (Wikipedia). Best route likely via GHO Capital (ghocapital.com) — no published personal contact found.

name: Kavita Singhania
current_role: Shareholder (~5%) in J.K. Cement Ltd; director of Express Infrastructure (Chennai real-estate developer)
profile: Kavita Yadupati Singhania holds a stake in listed J.K. Cement, run until his 2020 death by her husband Yadupati Singhania as chairman & MD. She briefly served as a non-executive director of J.K. Cement (2020-21) and is a director of Chennai developer Express Infrastructure; she has no operating role in the cement business.

name: Manny Stul
current_role: Co-owner of Moose Toys (Melbourne); former chairman/co-CEO — current formal title not confirmed (stepson Paul Solomon became Executive Chairman, Ronnie Frankowski CEO, Oct 2025)
profile: Born in a German refugee camp to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivors, Stul grew up in Western Australia, built and listed giftware firm Skansen, then in 2000 took over struggling Moose Toys and grew sales ~7,000% on hits like Shopkins (1bn+ units sold) and Mighty Beanz. Moose remains Melbourne-headquartered and family-owned.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he became the first Australian to win EY World Entrepreneur of the Year, aged 67. During the pandemic logistics crunch he chartered an entire ship to bring Moose products from China.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of university and worked in construction to fund his first business, giftware company Skansen, founded in 1973 and publicly listed 20 years later for over A$15m. As a toddler he spent three years in the Northam migrant camp in Western Australia.
notes: Moose leadership reshuffle Oct 2025 (https://globaltoynews.com/2025/10/09/moose-names-frankowski-ceo-other-management-changes/). Wife Jacqui Tobias is a long-time Moose product lead. Northam camp detail from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Stul).

notes: Lane spelling 'Lagnera' = Lagüera. Death confirmed by FEMSA press release (https://www.femsa.com/en/press-room/press-release/fundacion-paz-es-a-b-p-recognizes-the-life-and-legacy-of-eugenio-garza-laguera/) and Wikipedia. Family stake passed to daughter Eva Gonda de Rivera's branch.

name: Michaela Herz
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltungs SE (Herz family holding, Hamburg)
profile: Granddaughter of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and daughter of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for ~35 years. After Günter and his sister sold their Tchibo stake in 2003 they founded Mayfair, a Hamburg family holding investing in companies, bonds and real estate; Michaela owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions.
interesting_fact: Mayfair's first big deal was a 17% (later 27%) stake in Puma in 2004, sold to PPR at €330/share; it then bought Germanischer Lloyd for €575m, which expanded into oil & gas and renewable-energy services before merging into DNV GL in 2013 (stake sold 2017).
notes: Extremely private — almost no public footprint under her own name. Energy angle for the podcast: Mayfair's Germanischer Lloyd/DNV GL investment. Aunt Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel's branch has exited Mayfair (Forbes). Mayfair website did not load; no published contact found.

current_role: Minority shareholder in Pidilite Industries; no executive role found
profile: Kalpana Parekh is the only daughter of Balvant Parekh (d. 2013), founder of Pidilite Industries, India's leading adhesives and sealants maker (Fevicol, M-Seal, Fevikwik). She holds a minority stake in the company, chaired by her brother Madhukar Parekh; she has no public operating role.

name: Patrick Fung Yuk-bun (冯钰斌)
current_role: Executive Director, King Fook Holdings (HKEX:280); former Chairman of OCBC Wing Hang Bank (to 2022)
profile: Hong Kong banker who led family-controlled Wing Hang Bank for decades — joined 1976, director 1980, CEO 1992, chairman & CEO from 1996 — and steered its 2014 sale to Singapore's OCBC, staying on as chairman of OCBC Wing Hang until 2022. He now sits on the board of jeweller King Fook Holdings (chairs its ESG committee) and Miramar Hotel.
interesting_fact: He spent nearly 50 years with one bank: from joining Wing Hang in 1976 through its 2014 sale to OCBC and his chairmanship of the renamed OCBC Wing Hang Bank until 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond banking he has served as an adjunct professor at Hong Kong PolyU's School of Accounting and Finance and on the Board of Governors of the Hong Kong Philharmonic Society.

public_contacts.value: irenquiry@kingfook.com (King Fook Holdings IR, company he is a director of)

notes: Not to be confused with barrister Patrick Fung SC. Wealth largely from the OCBC sale of Wing Hang (2014). Executive vs non-executive status at King Fook differs between 2025 and 2026 annual reports. Roles from 2016 article may be dated.

name: Anna Kasprzak
current_role: Co-owner of ECCO (Danish shoemaker) with mother Hanni and brother André; international dressage rider (recently competing as Anna Toosbuy Rasch)
profile: Granddaughter of ECCO founder Karl Toosbuy and daughter of owner Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak and former CEO Dieter Kasprzak; she co-owns the family shoe company, which sells in ~90 countries through 2,200+ stores. She is best known as a Danish Olympic dressage rider and runs a private dressage barn in Haderslev.
interesting_fact: She rode for Denmark at the 2012 and 2016 Olympics, finishing 4th with the team in London 2012 and 14th individually in Rio 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before her senior career she won one silver and six bronze medals at European junior and young-rider championships, and finished 5th at the 2016 Dressage World Cup final.
notes: Recent equestrian coverage lists her as 'Anna Toosbuy Rasch' (per eurodressage, 2025) — use that name when searching results. Private on business matters; ECCO corporate communications is the likely route. No published personal contact found.

name: Zelimkhan Mutsoev
current_role: Deputy of the Russian State Duma (United Russia), serving his 6th convocation (8th Duma, elected 2021)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1959) Russian businessman-politician of Yazidi heritage. He moved to Moscow in the early 1990s, ran a foreign-trade association, became a co-owner of Pervouralsk New Pipe Plant in 1998 and later built holdings in fertilizers (Uralkali stake) and real estate, while serving in the Duma almost continuously since 1999.
interesting_fact: He was dropped from the Duma after the 2011 election but returned in 2012 when another United Russia deputy resigned and her mandate was transferred to him.
notes: CAUTION: sitting Russian Duma deputy — likely subject to Western sanctions applied to Duma members since 2022 (not verified in this pass; check OFAC/EU/UK lists before any contact). Wikipedia also records a 2008 dispute over a Kyiv hotel. Probably not a suitable podcast guest.

name: Rishi Shah
current_role: None — former co-founder, chairman & CEO of Outcome Health (resigned 2018); sentenced in June 2024 to 7.5 years in prison for fraud
profile: Oak Brook, Illinois-born (1986) Northwestern dropout who co-founded ContextMedia (later Outcome Health) in 2006 to put health-education screens in doctors' waiting rooms; it hit a $5.6bn valuation in 2017. After a WSJ investigation he resigned, and in 2023 he was convicted of mail, wire and bank fraud and money laundering.

notes: NOT SUITABLE for outreach: convicted in April 2023 of fraud tied to a ~$1bn scheme and sentenced June 2024 to 7.5 years (Wikipedia). Rich-list wealth figure is stale.

name: Charles Ruggieri
current_role: Founder, Batipart (family real-estate/tourism/hotel investment group, Luxembourg); day-to-day led by his children Nicolas (CEO), Claire and Julien
profile: French property entrepreneur who spent 15+ years managing the housing stock of Lorraine's steel industry, took it independent as Batibail, merged it with Gecina in 1999 and grew Foncière des Régions (now Covivio) and the care-home group that became Korian. Batipart, founded 1988, now manages ~€4.5bn of real estate, tourism and hotel assets in Europe, Africa and North America, 100% family-controlled.
interesting_fact: Batipart was a French and European pioneer of large sale-and-leaseback deals in the 2000s and incubated what became Korian, one of Europe's largest care-home operators.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in social housing for Lorraine steelworkers: Batipart's name comes from 'Batigère-Participations', set up in 1988 to hold the group's staff profit-sharing stake. With his wife Marianne he founded the Fondation Juniclair (2007), which funds education, women's protection and environmental projects, committing to each region for at least 5 years.
notes: Family group values 'discretion and humility' — expect a private founder; route via Batipart (Luxembourg) or Nicolas Ruggieri. Batipart governance page lists him as founder (https://www.batipart.com/le-groupe/gouvernance/); alive status inferred from current site, no recent personal news found.

name: Yousuf Mohammad Salah Jamjoom
current_role: Founder and ~42% shareholder, Jamjoom Pharmaceuticals Factory Co. (Tadawul-listed, Jeddah); no longer listed on the current board
profile: Jeddah businessman who ran pharmaceutical distributor Jamjoom Medicine Store as CEO from 1965 to 2005 and founded Jamjoom Pharmaceuticals Factory, one of Saudi Arabia's largest makers of OTC and generic medicines, listed on the Saudi exchange in 2023. His sons now run the board: Mahmoud is chairman, Ahmed vice-chairman.
interesting_fact: He earned a diploma in commerce from the University of Wales back in 1947, and led Jamjoom Medicine Store for 40 years (1965-2005).
deep_cut_fact: The company he founded was the first in Saudi Arabia to build a complete soft-gelatin capsule manufacturing facility and pioneered Blow-Fill-Seal technology for sterile eye-care products in the Kingdom.
notes: Likely in his mid-90s (1947 diploma); 2025-26 board list on company site names only his sons (Mahmoud chairman, Ahmed vice-chair, Waleed/Alaa/Mohammed members). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source; approach via the family/chairman's office.
